newsitem.title: RUSSIA: N.Korean airline to start flying to Vladivostok.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean airline to start flying to Vladivostok.

text.p: Air Koryo, the state airline of North Korea, will begin flying passengers to the Russian Pacific port of Vladivostok, aviation officials in the city said on Wednesday.

Russian state-owned airline Vladivostok-Avia had said it would not exercise its right to block the already-granted federal approval of the new route from Pyongyang, Vladivostok-Avia's finance director, Alexei Katashonov, told Reuters.
A starting date should be announced soon, he added.
Katashonov also said several Chinese carriers, a Taiwanese airline, Germany's Lufthansa and Finland's Finnair were also interested in flying to Valdivostok.
He said that Lufthansa had suggested extending its Frankfurt-Novosibirsk route to Vladivostok.
A spokeswoman for Lufthansa in Moscow, however, said the company did not plan to begin talks with Vladivostok-Avia before the end of the year. She declined to comment further.
Katashonov said federal authorities in Moscow, worried about diplomatic ties with China, were withholding approval for flights from Taiwan.
Vladivostok-Avia had 1996 pretax profit of 10 billion roubles, up from six billion in 1995.
The company operates four Ilyushin Il-76 freighters and three Tupolev Tu-154 and 11 Yakovlev Yak-40 passenger jets. The company fleet also includes 17 helicopters.
Vladivostok-Avia plans to open new routes to Irkutsk in Siberia, Yekaterinburg in the Urals, Seoul and Pusan in South Korea and several destinations in Japan later this year.
